profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a legal research consultancy supporting a comparative media-law article and expert appendix on pre-2010 Indonesia–Malaysia cross-border broadcasting. The team is splitting work between a regulatory analysis workstream and a source-compilation workstream, and they need to align on handoffs for the comparative legal matrix, border-enforcement examples, translations, and the shared evidence folder. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the regulatory matrix, which historical examples will anchor the legal discussion, what counts as the 'final source pack,' and how updated materials will be uploaded for the authors' next draft. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on deliverables, timing, and shared resources before the Friday circulation deadline.

members.name: Farah Lim
members.expertise: Comparative broadcasting regulation, administrative enforcement, legal source synthesis
members.background: Malaysia-qualified lawyer who previously clerked on communications-regulation matters and now supervises cross-jurisdiction legal research for academic and expert-report projects.
members.private_state: She wants a concise, reviewable legal appendix that can be checked quickly by the authors without reopening the scope of the paper, and she is trying to avoid the team getting bogged down in archival materials that are hard to verify formally.
hidden_assumptions: The 'regulatory matrix' should include only formally binding instruments such as statutes, published regulations, and reported decisions, not ministry circulars or board guidance.
When they refer to the 'border-reception examples,' they mean documented over-the-air spillover and official enforcement responses that can be tied directly to state control of broadcasting.
A 'final source pack' is final for internal author review if it has stable citations, working English translations, and enough primary text to support the legal narrative.
Uploading the 'latest version to the drive' means updating the existing master spreadsheet and replacing prior drafts so everyone looks at one current set.

members.name: Aditya Pranowo
members.role: Senior Associate, Indonesia Research & Source Coordination
members.expertise: Indonesian media law, archival legal materials, bilingual source tracing
members.background: Indonesia-qualified associate who has spent several years assembling historical statutory and enforcement records for regional media-law matters, especially where formal law and agency practice diverge.
members.private_state: He wants the appendix to reflect how media control actually operated on the ground and is quietly trying to protect against later challenges from reviewers who may ask for fuller documentary support and original-language extracts.
hidden_assumptions: The 'regulatory matrix' should capture all operative control instruments, including circulars, censorship-board directives, licensing guidance, and other quasi-formal materials that shaped enforcement in practice.

The 'border-reception examples' include piracy-related seizures, satellite-dish restrictions, and antenna reception near Batam, Nunukan, Sabah, and similar border zones because those are all part of cross-border media flow.
A 'final source pack' is final only when it is ready to circulate outside the immediate legal team, with original-language scans, translation excerpts, and pin-cited supporting pages.
Uploading the 'latest versions to the drive' means adding dated folders and preserving prior files so the authors can trace source provenance and translation history.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the regulatory matrix
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'put it in the regulatory matrix.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the matrix should contain only formal legal authorities: enacted statutes, published regulations, and citable decisions.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the matrix should also include circulars, censorship guidelines, licensing directives, and other non-statutory instruments that affected actual control of cross-border content.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In media-law practice, both formal and quasi-formal materials are casually discussed as 'instruments' or 'controls,' so the phrase sounds fully aligned even though the boundary of inclusion is different.

misalignment_points.topic: Which cross-border examples will anchor the appendix
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to 'the border-reception examples' or 'the border file.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of documented broadcast spillover and official responses tied to lawful reception near the Malaysia–Indonesia border, especially examples that map neatly onto state control of broadcasting.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the broader set of cross-border intake mechanisms discussed in the study, including piracy incidents, satellite-dish usage, and antenna capture in multiple border regions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The study itself groups several modes of cross-border exchange under a common theme, so using one broad label for the examples feels natural and does not prompt either person to enumerate the specific incidents in mind.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a final source pack
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that Aditya will send the 'final source pack' on Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a lawyer-ready internal package: stable citation list, workable translations, and enough extracts for the authors to review substance before polishing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a circulation-ready package: scanned originals, bilingual excerpts, traceable provenance, and page-specific support that could survive external scrutiny.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Status labels like 'final' are routine workflow shorthand, and each person assumes the other's standard is the obvious professional default for a high-stakes legal research deliverable.

misalignment_points.topic: How updated materials will be uploaded
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree to 'upload the latest versions to the drive.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a single master spreadsheet and refreshed linked files to be overwritten so the team always sees one current set.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to add new dated folders with separate PDFs, translation notes, and prior versions preserved for provenance and comparison.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Shared-drive practices are usually inherited from prior team habits rather than discussed explicitly, and 'latest version' sounds operationally clear even when version-control methods differ.
